title: Ab initio path integral Monte Carlo study of the 2D uniform electron liquid at finite temperatures
authors: Tobias Dornheim, Fotios Kalkavouras, Paul Hamann, Zhandos A. Moldabekov, Jan Vorberger, Panagiotis Tolias
abstract: We present extensive \emph{ab initio} path integral Monte Carlo (PIMC) simulations of the two-dimensional uniform electron gas (2DEG), covering a broad range of density parameters $r_s=0.1,\dots,50$ and temperatures $Θ=k_\textnormal{B}T/E_\textnormal{Fermi}=0.5,\dots,16$. This allows us to analyze various structural, linear density response and spectral properties. We find clear evidence of a \emph{roton-type} feature in the dynamic structure factor at strong coupling and intermediate wavenumbers. We also benchmark novel dielectric theory implementations for the 2DEG~[Kalkavouras \emph{et al.}~arXiv:2601.14989] for structural and spectral properties across the liquid phase diagram. The PIMC results can be used to benchmark existing theories and approximations, and guide the development of new methodologies.
summary: This work performs extensive Path Integral Monte Carlo simulations on the 2D uniform electron gas across wide ranges of density and temperature. By analyzing the imaginary-time correlation function, the authors report finding a roton-type feature indicative of strong electronic correlations. The results are designed to rigorously test and improve theoretical models describing quantum liquid behavior.
main_problem: To analyze the structural, linear density response, and spectral properties of the two-dimensional uniform electron liquid (2DEG) at finite temperatures.
main_result: The study finds clear evidence of a roton-type feature in the dynamic structure factor at strong coupling and intermediate wavenumbers. These PIMC results serve to benchmark existing theories for the 2DEG.
method: Ab initio Path Integral Monte Carlo (PIMC) simulations are used extensively, analyzing the imaginary-time density–density correlation function (ITCF).
model_or_system: The physical system is the two-dimensional uniform electron gas (2DEG), treated as a quantum many-body system in the jellium approximation. The simulation covers a wide range of densities ($r_s=0.1$ to $50$) and temperatures ($\Theta=0.5$ to $16$).
key_observables: Static structure factor S(q), static linear density response $\chi(q)$, and the imaginary-time density–density correlation function F(q, $\tau$).
important_parameters: Density parameter $r_s$, temperature ratio $\Theta = k_BT/E_{Fermi}$, and momentum transfer $q$.
main_assumptions: The analysis avoids the exponentially ill-conditioned analytic continuation problem by working directly in the imaginary-time domain. The fermionic nature requires specialized sampling techniques to handle the sign problem.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates a PIMC configuration in the $\tau$-$x$-plane, showing the free propagator and the estimation of F(q, $\tau$).
paper_structure: The paper details the use of PIMC to calculate correlation functions by working in imaginary time. It presents results across various density and temperature regimes, focusing on identifying collective excitations like the roton feature.
why_interesting: While focused on electron liquids, the rigorous application of advanced Monte Carlo techniques (PIMC) to study emergent collective modes (rotons) provides valuable methodological insights applicable to strongly correlated quantum systems in general.

FIG. 2. The PIMC convergence with the number of imaginary-time propagators P for the 2DEG at rs = 30 and Θ = 0.5 with N = 14. Left: static structure factor S(q) for P = 1000 (blue diamonds), P = 500 (yellow squares), P = 200 (black circles) and P = 100 (red crosses). The inset shows the differences with the reference results for P = 1000. Right: same but for the thermal structure factor Sβ/2(q) = F(q, β/2).

FIG. 3. The static structure factor S(q) of the 2DEG at rs = 0.5 and Θ = 4, with N = 14 electrons. Red circles: standard PIMC results for P = 200; green crosses: configuration PIMC results [150]. The inset shows the relative difference between the two data sets.

FIG. 4. Wavenumber dependence of different ITCF F(q, τ) τ−slices for τ = 0 (crosses), τ = β/10 (diamonds) and τ = β/2 (squares). PIMC results for the 2DEG at rs = 0.5 and Θ = 4. The green and red colors distinguish simulation results with N = 34 and N = 14 electrons, respectively.

FIG. 5. Wavenumber dependence of different ITCF F(q, τ) τ−slices for τ = 0 (crosses), τ = β/10 (diamonds) and τ = β/2 (squares). PIMC results for the 2DEG at rs = 50 and Θ = 1. The yellow, green and red colors distinguish simulation results with N = 70, N = 34 and N = 14 electrons, respectively.
